- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend + negative sentiment, model may lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch reversal.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% in final 5–7 days.  
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; if sentiment shifts sharply, wait 1–2 days before adjusting forecast to avoid noise-driven overcorrection.
